source.title: Slower Generalization, Faster Memorization: A Sweet Spot in Algorithmic Learning
source.authors: Shinichiro So; Kyelim Lee; Albert No

record.file_problem: none; the full paper text is present
record.tranche_reason: The paper discusses double descent and reports dataset-size effects on optimizer updates to reach accuracy thresholds. It does not measure test error versus model size, training time, or sample size as specified by the claim versions.
record.gate_note: The paper measures update counts to reach train and validation accuracy thresholds while varying dataset size. Those are convergence-time results, not test-error curves against model size, epochs, or sample size. The random-suffix and train–random-gap results concern the paper's proposed mechanism and are not results on the claim versions.
record.test_reason: The study measures optimizer updates (and epochs) needed to reach train and validation exact-match thresholds as dataset size varies. It never reports test error against model size, epochs or sample size. The authors say the result is not about asymptotic accuracy, and Section 6 sets it apart from double-descent views. Double descent is only cited and discussed, so no version is tested.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. The authors conclude that NW validation thresholds are reached fastest, in optimizer updates, at an intermediate dataset size. They also report that partial rule learning can speed up training-set fitting, and that multiplication does not show the slowdown. The onset of generalization (critical data size) and the update-optimal dataset size are distinct.
record.recipe_differences: The study performs dataset-size sweeps and measures threshold-crossing times in structured-output tasks; it does not reproduce the original double-descent risk-versus-model-size experiment.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported pattern depends on task (NW versus arithmetic controls), dataset size, model depth, sequence length, threshold, and whether convergence is counted in optimizer updates or epochs. The sweet-spot location shifts with depth; epoch normalization yields a different data-size pattern.

fits_no_version.finding: In NW matrix generation, an intermediate dataset size minimizes optimizer updates to reach strict validation exact-match thresholds. Larger datasets generalize but need more updates.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In structured-output algorithmic tasks, update-based convergence speed can be non-monotonic in dataset size, distinct from test error or asymptotic accuracy.

fits_no_version.finding: In the partial-generalization band, more data reduces the updates needed to reach high training accuracy.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Partial rule learning can accelerate fitting, so more data can speed memorization.

fits_no_version.finding: Counted in epochs, larger datasets need fewer passes, so the sweet spot is specific to update counts.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The dataset-size sweet spot depends on measuring convergence in optimizer updates rather than epochs.

fits_no_version.finding: Multiplication and addition show no interior validation optimum.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The update-based intermediate-data optimum is task-dependent.

record.problems: The evidence is limited to small Transformers and synthetic algorithmic tasks. Exact crossing-time values are largely presented in plots rather than tabulated in the text, and the authors note that update-based results should not be interpreted as asymptotic accuracy or intrinsic harm from larger datasets.
record.rows_left_out: Random-suffix and train–random-gap outcomes were excluded because they concern the proposed mechanism rather than the claim versions. Exact plotted crossing-time values were not transcribed where the text gives only qualitative descriptions (Figures 1–11).

untested.parts: No sweep of test error against model size. Depth D∈{3,4,5,6} is varied only to check robustness of convergence timing.
No curves of test error over training time. Epoch-normalized results count epochs-to-threshold across dataset sizes.

Dataset size is swept, but the outcome is updates-to-threshold, not test error. Larger datasets still reach the validation threshold, just later; the authors say larger datasets are not shown to be worse.
No risk-versus-capacity curves across model classes.
No effective-complexity measure used to predict where a peak falls.
No label-noise or regularization sweep; weight decay is fixed at 0.1.
No re-counting of parameters or complexity.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's 'discusses/T6' is correct. The superficial link to V3 (more data can hurt) does not hold: the measure is time-to-threshold under a fixed 50k-update budget, not test error. Some large-N runs are censored at strict thresholds, which could be read as worse fixed-budget accuracy, but the paper does not report test error at a fixed budget. All rows correctly carry versions ['none'].

versions.untested_parts: No model-size sweep measuring test error; depth is varied while dataset-size convergence is examined.
No test-error trajectory over training epochs. Epoch-normalized analyses measure epochs to accuracy thresholds as dataset size varies.
The paper does not measure test error as sample size increases; it measures update-based time to reach validation-accuracy thresholds.
No risk-versus-capacity curves across model classes.
No single effective-complexity measure is tested as a predictor of peak location.
No label-noise or regularization sweep for double-descent peaks.
No re-counting of model complexity or test of whether that makes a second descent an ordinary U-shape.

rows.subject: decoder-only Transformer (D=6)
rows.operation_detail: Swept NW training-set size and measured optimizer updates to validation exact-match thresholds.

conditions.value: multiple exact-match thresholds; strict threshold τ=0.98

rows.measure: Optimizer updates to reach validation exact-match accuracy threshold
rows.value: Validation crossing time is non-monotonic in dataset size; intermediate datasets converge fastest, and larger datasets still generalize but require more updates.
rows.uncertainty: Five random seeds per configuration; plots report one standard deviation, numerical uncertainty not stated.
rows.note: The reported outcome is update-based convergence time, not test error as a function of sample size.

rows.subject: decoder-only Transformers (D ∈ {3, 4, 5, 6})
rows.size_stated: Depths D=3, 4, 5, and 6; embedding dimension 64D; feed-forward width 256D
rows.operation_detail: Repeated the NW dataset-size sweep across model depths and measured training and validation threshold-crossing updates.
rows.measure: Optimizer updates to reach train and validation exact-match thresholds
rows.value: Across depths, validation crossing time is non-monotonic in N; in the partial-generalization band, training crossing time can decrease as N grows. The sweet-spot location shifts with depth.
rows.uncertainty: Five random seeds per configuration; one standard deviation shown in seed-variability plots; numerical uncertainty not stated.
rows.locator: Sections 4.3 and 7; Figures 2 and 6; Appendix C
rows.note: The paper reports the cross-depth pattern qualitatively; this does not establish epoch-wise double descent.

rows.subject: decoder-only Transformers (D ∈ {3, 4, 5, 6})
rows.operation_detail: Re-expressed the same threshold-crossing results in epochs rather than optimizer updates.
rows.measure: Epochs to train and validation accuracy thresholds as dataset size varies
rows.value: Epoch normalization emphasizes data exposure and recovers a more conventional view in which larger datasets require fewer passes over the data.
rows.note: This varies dataset size and measures epochs-to-threshold; it does not measure error over training epochs.

rows.subject: three-digit multiplication model
rows.operation_detail: Swept dataset size and measured optimizer updates to validation accuracy thresholds.
rows.measure: Optimizer updates to reach validation exact-match thresholds
rows.value: Validation curves remain roughly flat or improve with dataset size; the paper reports no pronounced post-threshold slowdown.
rows.uncertainty: Five random seeds per configuration; numerical uncertainty not stated.
rows.note: This is a task contrast for update-based convergence, not a test-error-versus-sample-size result.

rows.subject: addition model
rows.operation_detail: Swept dataset size and compared train and validation threshold-crossing updates.
rows.measure: Optimizer updates to reach train and validation exact-match thresholds
rows.value: Train and validation crossings remain close; the paper reports no interior validation optimum for addition.
rows.uncertainty: Five random seeds per configuration unless otherwise stated; numerical uncertainty not stated.
rows.note: Task-scope control; the figure's exact crossing values are not stated in the text.

rows.subject: decoder-only Transformers (D ∈ {3, 4, 5, 6})
rows.operation_detail: Repeated the NW dataset-size sweep at sequence length L=4 and measured threshold-crossing time.
rows.measure: Optimizer updates to reach train and validation exact-match thresholds
rows.value: Validation convergence is non-monotonic in N; the decrease in training crossing time appears around the onset of weak validation thresholds.
rows.uncertainty: Seed-variance plots report one standard deviation; numerical uncertainty not stated.
rows.note: Robustness result on convergence timing, not on test error versus dataset size.
